extracted.intended_audience: researchers, institutional administrators, and nonprofit organizations seeking Burroughs Wellcome Fund (BWF) grants
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of Burroughs Wellcome Fund funding opportunities, eligibility, review process, priorities, and application requirements for institutional nominees and nonprofit grant seekers. Covers program types, topic focus areas, and procedural rules (deadlines, nomination, tax status, advisory committees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Burroughs Wellcome Fund’s grantmaking strategies support biomedical scientists at the beginning of their careers and areas of science that are poised for significant advancement but are currently undervalued and underfunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs target early-career biomedical researchers and undervalued/underfunded scientific frontiers; applicants/projects aligned with these priorities are the Fund's focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program types supported
rubrics_metrics.description: BWF has programs which support primary and secondary students, science and mathematics teachers, institutions, and academic scientists: postdoctoral-faculty bridging awards and faculty awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should identify the program type that matches their role (K-12, graduate students, postdocs, faculty, institutions, teachers) and apply to that specific program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: BWF funds opportunities across topic areas including Biomedical Sciences, Career Guidance, Climate Change, Diversity in Science, Infectious Disease, Institutional Programs, Interfaces in Science, Regulatory Science, Reproductive Science, and Science Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and proposals should align with one or more of these stated focus areas; program pages provide further detail on topics and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary awardee is institution (degree-granting) in US/Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of the BWF’s grantmaking is through competitive award programs. Most awards are made to degree-granting institutions in the United States and Canada on behalf of individual researchers, who must be nominated by their institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual researchers are generally nominated by and funded through their degree-granting institutions; independent individual applications are not the typical mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination requirement by institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual researchers must be nominated by their institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should work with their institutional administration to secure nomination and submission; check program-specific nomination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-exempt status requirement (501(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: All institutions receiving awards must be tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions that are not 501(c)(3) in the U.S. are ineligible to receive awards; applicants should verify institutional tax status before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and submission time
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be submitted no later than 4:00 p.m., Eastern Time, on the deadline date provided for the indicated program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to deadline date and 4:00 p.m. ET cutoff; follow program pages for exact deadline dates and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific guidelines and application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for the competitive award programs, select the program below and follow the guidelines and application requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each program has its own detailed guidelines—applicants must consult and comply with program-specific eligibility, materials, formats, and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committees as external peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program has an Advisory Committee consisting of members who are external peer reviewers that lend their expertise and time to reviewing and assessing applications for BWF programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be evaluated by external experts convened by BWF; prepare submissions with the expectation of peer review standards of scientific and educational merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of advisory committee members for expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: BWF selects members of these committees for their scientific and educational expertise in the program areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee composition is expertise-driven; applicants should present clear scientific/educational rationale so committee members can assess fit and merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview and recommendation stage for some programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee meets, for some programs, to interview potential nominees, and make recommendations based on their experiences to the BWF Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain competitions include an interview stage; nominees may be interviewed by advisory committees prior to recommendation to the Board—prepare for possible interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committees are separate from the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the various advisory committees are complete and separate bodies from the BWF Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory committee recommendations inform but are institutionally distinct from Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ad hoc noncompetitive grants to nonprofits
rubrics_metrics.description: To complement these competitive award programs, we also make modest grants on an “ad hoc” basis to nonprofit organizations conducting activities intended to improve the general environment for science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These noncompetitive grants are modest, ad hoc, and intended for nonprofits whose activities closely relate to BWF focus areas; consult BWF for opportunities and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/programmatic partnership for K-12 in North Carolina
rubrics_metrics.description: The Burroughs Wellcome Fund is committed to supporting science education for primary and secondary students and has partnered with various organizations to help develop an infrastructure for improving science, mathematics, and technology education across North Carolina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K-12 science education efforts may include targeted partnerships or initiatives with geographic focus (e.g., North Carolina); check program details for localized opportunities.
